entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mikołaj Kamieniecki h. Pilawa (died April 25, 1515) was a foundational figure in the military history of the Jagiellonian Kingdom of Poland, serving as the first Great Hetman of the Crown. His appointment in 1503 by King Alexander Jagiellon marked a pivotal institutional development, formalizing a permanent commander-in-chief for the Polish military and establishing a critical precedent for the future organization of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's armed forces. Kamieniecki's career unfolded during a period of intense geopolitical flux in Central and Eastern Europe, characterized by the rising threats from the Ottoman Empire, the Grand Duchy of Moscow, and persistent tensions with the Teutonic Order, underscoring the necessity for a strong, unified military command.

Throughout his tenure, Kamieniecki distinguished himself in numerous military engagements, primarily defending the southern and eastern borders of the Polish Crown. He played a significant role in the Polish-Moldavian War (1497-1498), leading forces against Stephen III of Moldavia, and later commanded Polish armies against Tartar incursions in Podolia. His most notable campaigns involved confronting Ottoman expansionism, including his successful defense against a major Ottoman invasion in 1509 at the Battle of Chocim (Khotyn), where he decisively repelled the invading forces. He also served as Castellan of Sandomierz from 1507 and Voivode of Sandomierz from 1511, consolidating his influence within the royal administration.

entities.summary:
Mikołaj Kamieniecki (c. 1460 – April 25, 1515), born in Odrzykoń, emerged as a preeminent military figure in late 15th and early 16th century Poland, serving as the inaugural Great Hetman of the Crown. His career unfolded during a period of intense geopolitical flux, characterized by the expansionist pressures of the Ottoman Empire, the Crimean Khanate, and the Grand Duchy of Moscow on the eastern frontiers of the Jagiellonian realm. Kamieniecki's military prowess and organizational acumen were instrumental in solidifying the nascent structure of the Polish professional army, transforming ad hoc levies into a more cohesive defensive force against persistent external threats.

His command was marked by a series of critical engagements that defined Poland's eastern policy. In 1509, Kamieniecki led Polish forces to a decisive victory against the Moldavian army at the Battle of Chocim (Hotin), securing the southeastern border. He subsequently played a crucial role in repelling Tatar incursions, most notably orchestrating the victory at the Battle of Wiśniowiec in 1512, which significantly curbed the destructive raids of the Crimean Khanate into Podolia and Ruthenia. These campaigns, alongside his strategic defense of key fortifications like Kamieniec Podolski, underscored the necessity of a standing military command and directly contributed to the formalization of the hetmanate as a permanent institution within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's administrative framework.
